bug_semantics: CWE-835 infinite loop: a crafted CFB file with a LeftSiblingID/RightSiblingID cycle makes Storage.EnumerateEntries() and Storage.OpenStream() hang with no exception.
flaw_origin: OpenMcdf3 first replaced linear FAT directory-sector enumeration with an unguarded Left/Right sibling-tree walk in DirectoryTreeEnumerator (MoveNext/PushLeft). Parent Storage walked directory sectors and would terminate; the new stack walk never tracks visited IDs. DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry (92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344) later added a second unguarded BST sibling walk used by OpenStream; that is a follow-on rewrite of the same missing cycle check, not the first write.
ai_marker: absent — no AI marker in the BIC commit object (author/committer human; no AI trailers), verified via cat-file during case analysis
evidence: GHSA-jxpf-xq2m-q525 / CVE-2026-41511 (bundle withdrawn_at null; first patched 3.1.3) cites 24f445a557fc4f46461cf6d02d296cce16c293a0, which adds Brent cycle detection to OpenMcdf/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs (throw FileFormatException on loop). That SHA is an ancestor of tag v3.1.3. BIC b2fc989e4c3e6b682c8416bf5aa72b3fe37ae9e3 (single parent 7821a5d148cb523d1f3c347680c5eeccc25de3e3) adds OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs whose PushLeft follows LeftSiblingID and MoveNext follows RightSiblingID with no visited set; Storage.EnumerateDirectoryEntries and OpenStream both used that enumerator. git cat-file -e 7821a5d148cb523d1f3c347680c5eeccc25de3e3:OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs fails; parent Storage.cs enumerates FAT directory sectors linearly. git cat-file -p on the BIC shows author/committer Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com> with subject Allow storage directory entry enumeration and no Co-Authored-By / Generated-with / bot author. Later 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 first adds DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry (unguarded sibling walk) but rewrites rather than first-introduces the cycle-vulnerable traversal.
reasoning: Re-adjudicated BLOCKED -> NOT_AI after independent recheck (protocol-recheck-disagreements-20260829.md) and git re-verification, 2026-08-29. Basis: Git-verified 2026-08-29 in openmcdf clone: OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs absent at parent 7821a5d148; BIC b2fc989e4c first writes the sibling-cycle walk; advisory fix 24f445a5 is ancestor of v3.1.3. Original analysis retained for provenance: The advisory's exploit begins with attacker-controlled directory IDs and reaches traversal code that assumes the directory graph is acyclic. Source history shows that assumption in the package's first implementation: SourceForge SVN r4 recursively follows both sibling directions with no cycle guard, while its immediate parent r3 is empty. The assigned Git history starts weeks later with an aggregate snapshot already containing those lines, so that root cannot honestly be labeled the smallest BIC. The v3 stack traversal introduced by b2fc989e is independently vulnerable but is a later reimplementation of the established flaw. For fixes, the advisory-linked 24f445a5 lands exactly in v3.1.3 and adds Brent detection to enumeration; source inspection shows lookup remained unguarded there, and c6f82db7 in v3.1.4 supplies traversal-wide validation and exact cycle regression coverage, making it the complete two-path fix. The actual r4 BIC record has no AI marker, but it is an SVN revision with no full 40-hex Git object or 40-hex parent. Because the required closed verdict cannot substitute a later migration snapshot or rewrite for the smallest BIC, the correct result is BLOCKED at the VCS-history boundary rather than NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Re-adjudicated: none — see reasoning prefix. Original gap: The precise unreachable fact is a full lowercase 40-hex Git commit ID (and 40-hex Git parent) for the true BIC, SourceForge SVN r4. First-party SVN proves r4 added the vulnerable recursion and r3 lacked it, but the assigned Git clone begins the legacy source at later no-parent snapshot 4e50280574bd50ed1fb37498e065c5f27dd5bb35 and contains no object representing r4. Closing as NOT_AI would require inventing a Git mapping or incorrectly treating that aggregate snapshot or the 2024 v3 rewrite as the smallest BIC. Separately, the advisory's stated 3.1.3 patched boundary is only partial for its two described paths; the complete lookup-plus-enumeration fix first appears in v3.1.4 via c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7.
